title: Support-dimension vanishing for sheaf Ext
statement: Let $X$ be a regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) of finite dimension $d$ [def-pc-dimension], and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. For every integer $q\geq0$ the support $\{x\in X: \mathcal Ext^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)_x\neq0\}$ of the sheaf Ext [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext] has Krull dimension at most $d-q$ as a subspace of $X$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (it is empty if $q>d$), and $H^p(X,\mathcal Ext^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G))=0$ [pqf-def-cohomology] for every integer $p>d-q$.

proof.text: Fix x in X and write d_x = dim O_{X,x}. The stalk isomorphism [lem-sc-ext-stalk-localization] identifies SheafExt^q(F,G)_x with Ext^q_{O_{X,x}}(F_x,G_x). Regularity of X makes O_{X,x} a regular local ring, and coherence makes F_x finitely generated; therefore [lem-sc-regular-local-ext-vanishing] gives SheafExt^q(F,G)_x = 0 whenever q > d_x.

source.place: Lemma lemma-Ext-0-regular (Tag 0FZ3), proof of (1), local Ext calculation

proof.text: Assume q <= d and let S be the support of SheafExt^q(F,G). S is closed in X: SheafExt^q(F,G) is coherent by [lem-sc-sheaf-ext-coherent], hence quasi-coherent of finite type by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], and its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. Hence an irreducible closed subset of S is an irreducible closed subset of X and its generic point lies in S, so by Step 1 its local ring has dimension d_x >= q. Let Z_0 < Z_1 < ... < Z_k be a chain of irreducible closed subsets of S, and x the generic point of Z_k. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] there is a chain Z_k = W_0 < W_1 < ... < W_{d_x} of irreducible closed subsets of X (d_x is finite since d_x <= d). Concatenating gives a chain of length k + d_x >= k + q starting at Z_0 = closure of its generic point x_0, so the same node gives dim O_{X,x_0} >= k+q, while dim O_{X,x_0} <= d by [def-pc-dimension]. Thus k <= d-q, i.e. S has topological Krull dimension at most d-q [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Lemma lemma-Ext-0-regular (Tag 0FZ3), proof of (1), sentences after the local Ext calculation

proof.text: X is Noetherian, S is closed of topological Krull dimension at most d-q by Step 2, and the underlying abelian sheaf of SheafExt^q(F,G) has support S (the stalks of the module and of its underlying abelian sheaf are the same colimit [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). Applying [lem-sc-support-dimension-cohomology-vanishing] with Z = S and r = d-q gives H^p(X, SheafExt^q(F,G)_ab) = 0 for every p > d-q, the cohomology of [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], which for the Zariski space of X is H^p(X_Zar, -). By [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] this group is isomorphic to H^p(X, SheafExt^q(F,G)) computed in O_X-modules [pqf-def-cohomology], so the latter vanishes for p > d-q.

source.place: Lemma lemma-Ext-0-regular (Tag 0FZ3), proof of (1), final paragraph; Cohomology Proposition Tag 02UZ

proof.text: If q > d, Step 1 makes every stalk zero because d_x <= d, so the sheaf Ext is zero and its cohomology is zero. Thus in all cases H^p(X, SheafExt^q(F,G)) = 0 for p > d-q.
